security_audit.summary: Six static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, path formatting, or a Mermaid code fence. Two Python examples execute Git with an unvalidated branch value split into arguments, creating command-argument injection risk if adopted. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or other semantic threat was found.

remediation.issue: The subprocess examples construct Git arguments by splitting a string containing an unvalidated base branch.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the branch as a Git ref, resolve it to a commit identifier, and pass a fixed argument array to subprocess.run.

content.user_title: Improve Pull Requests for Faster Reviews
content.value_statement: Large or unclear pull requests slow reviews and hide important risks. This skill creates structured descriptions, checklists, risk assessments, and split recommendations from change context.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes changed files and change statistics from Git diff information.
Builds structured pull request descriptions covering purpose, changes, testing, dependencies, and breaking changes.
Generates review checklists tailored to source, test, configuration, documentation, and security changes.
Estimates review effort, evaluates risk factors, and recommends ways to split large pull requests.
Produces Mermaid architecture diagrams, test coverage comparisons, and reviewer response templates when relevant.
limitations: Relies on complete repository context, commit history, and test data supplied by the user or available environment.
Example analyzers contain placeholder helper functions and are not a complete executable package.
Generated risk and coverage conclusions require verification with project-specific tools and policies.
Git operations and branch changes require user approval and a clean, correctly configured repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Pull Request
use_cases.description: Turn a feature diff, commit list, and test results into a focused description and reviewer checklist.

use_cases.title: Plan Reviews for Large Changes
use_cases.description: Assess change size and risk, then identify logical pull request splits and review priorities.

use_cases.title: Verify Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Compare testing, coverage, dependencies, and documentation before approving a release pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pull Request Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a clear pull request description for these changes: [summary]. Include purpose, key changes, testing, risks, and a reviewer checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a concise change summary and needs a complete description.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Diff and Commit List
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request diff and commit list: [details]. Group changes by category, identify missing context, and propose a focused review checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants structured review guidance from repository evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Large Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this large pull request: [diff and statistics]. Estimate review effort, identify risk factors, and recommend logical splits with dependencies between them.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead needs a staged review plan for an oversized change.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complete Review Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare base and head coverage data, architecture notes, and dependency changes: [details]. Produce a complete review package with evidence-based risks and Mermaid diagrams.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs coordinated documentation, metrics, diagrams, and risk analysis.

output_examples.input: A feature adds passwordless sign-in, updates API routes, and includes integration tests.
output_examples.output: Summary: Adds passwordless sign-in through new API routes. Risk: Medium because authentication behavior changes. Review focus: token expiry, fallback behavior, and integration tests.

output_examples.input: A refactor touches 35 files and 1,400 lines across the API, database, and tests.
output_examples.output: The change is large. Split database changes first, API refactoring second, and tests last. Keep each pull request independently reviewable.

output_examples.input: Line coverage falls from 88 percent to 84 percent after a dependency update.
output_examples.output: Coverage decreased by four points. Review uncovered dependency paths and add focused tests before merging.

best_practices: Provide the target branch, diff, commit intent, test results, and repository conventions before requesting analysis.
Verify generated metrics and risk claims against actual Git, coverage, and continuous integration results.
Keep descriptions factual and link each reviewer concern to a specific change or test.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generated coverage numbers or risk scores without checking their sources.
Do not combine unrelated changes only to avoid creating multiple pull requests.
Do not run branch-changing or push commands without confirming the repository state and user intent.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my repository?
faq.answer: The core output is guidance and documentation. Some playbook examples use Git commands, so execution requires explicit approval and repository checks.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the target branch, diff, commit messages, test results, coverage data, issue context, and repository review rules.

faq.question: Can it generate different pull request formats?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes structures for features, bug fixes, refactors, checklists, risk reports, and review responses.

faq.question: Can it measure test coverage?
faq.answer: It can format and compare supplied coverage data. It cannot create reliable coverage results without running the project test tooling.

faq.question: Can it create architecture diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft Mermaid diagrams when the provided context clearly describes architectural changes.

faq.question: Does it replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. Generated descriptions, checks, and risk assessments require validation by reviewers who understand the codebase and delivery requirements.
